definitions.meaning: pretty in the sense of attractive or flattering
the philosophical sense: coming into being, the process of change found everywhere in the natural world

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests something pretty and commonplace; it is two separate senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Becoming means attractive or flattering, and in philosophy it names the universal natural process of coming to be.

clue.text: College set on having Sunday off

indicators.note: off says a piece is removed from the words before it

parts.note: taken as written as one run; that the letters also sit inside it is a coincidence, since 'Sunday off' tells you to drop its S

explanation.surface: A college is being set upon, but at least not on a Sunday.
explanation.walkthrough: Write SET ON as one run, SETON, then take away the S that 'Sunday' gives.
explanation.definitionFit: Eton is the famous English public school, formally Eton College, near Windsor.

indicators.note: re- here means the letters are routed again, in a new order

explanation.surface: A diversion where the traffic has been sent another way.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this clue to the next only for the surface; 'Re-' prefixes a rearrangement of ROUTED.
explanation.definitionFit: A detour is a roundabout route taken instead of the usual one, the same thing as a road diversion.

indicators.note: awkward suggests the letters are clumsily arranged and must be put right

explanation.surface: Continuing the traffic story, the diversion takes you near some awkward stretch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part' looks like a noun but is the verb: to separate people.
explanation.definitionFit: To estrange people is to drive them apart, so as a verb it matches separating or parting.

clue.text: Sailor, soldier and girl join in dance

parts.note: a tar is an old word for a sailor
a soldier ant, hence ANT
Ella is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A sailor, a soldier and a girl get up to dance together.
explanation.definitionFit: The tarantella is a fast whirling Italian folk dance from southern Italy.

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some Chinese fruit grown in the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: The litchi, more often spelt lychee, is a sweet Chinese tropical fruit.

clue.text: Were they ruffled after she dressed?

indicators.note: dressed suggests the letters are arranged or put in order afresh

explanation.surface: A question about whether someone's composure was disturbed after she got dressed.
explanation.walkthrough: Ruffled feathers are the picture; the def is the question 'were they ruffled'.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds ruffle their plumage, and ruffled feathers is the idiom for being upset.

definitions.meaning: a senior hospital nurse is called by this title in Britain
Ophelia in Hamlet is the sibling of Laertes, a female sibling

explanation.walkthrough: In British hospitals a senior nurse is a 'Sister'.
explanation.definitionFit: A ward sister is a senior nurse, and Ophelia is Laertes' female sibling in Hamlet.

indicators.note: ruined suggests the act's letters are wrecked and rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A performer's act spoiled by interference.
explanation.definitionFit: Static is the crackling interference heard on a radio or phone line.

parts.note: feathers drift gently earthwards, and soft fluffy feathers have their own name too

explanation.walkthrough: Two senses combine: the direction things fall, and the soft under-plumage of birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Down is the direction of falling and also soft fine feathers.

indicators.note: performed suggests the letters are put on in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Native American braves once performed this ritual.
explanation.definitionFit: An observance is a rite or ceremony kept as a custom.

indicators.note: out of says one piece is removed from the other

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.definitionFit: Limber means supple and flexible, much the same as agile.

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are spread about into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A country where blades are hung out.
explanation.definitionFit: Bangladesh is a country in South Asia, east of India.

clue.text: A German mug? No, a genius

parts.note: the German word for 'a' is ein
a stein is a German beer mug

explanation.surface: Is he a German mug? No, he is a genius.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mug' tempts as a fool, set against 'genius'; it is the beer mug.
explanation.definitionFit: Albert Einstein's name has become a byword for a genius.

clue.text: Oliver F. Winchester was a killer

definitions.meaning: Winchester was a maker of rifles, a man in the firearms business

explanation.walkthrough: The rifle maker's surname evokes the famous rifle; read the word as two halves for the first sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A gunman is an armed killer, and a rifle maker is literally a firearms man.

clue.text: Love lies bleeding, but it never fades

definitions.meaning: love-lies-bleeding is a garden plant with drooping red tassels
in poetry, an imaginary flower that never withers

explanation.walkthrough: 'Love lies bleeding' reads as a tragic sentence but is a plant name.
explanation.definitionFit: Love-lies-bleeding belongs to this plant genus, whose poetic name means an unfading flower.

parts.note: the Med is short for the Mediterranean Sea
a lar is a Roman household god

explanation.surface: A sea god produces some fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The medlar is a small brown fruit eaten when half-rotten.

clue.text: What a crashed car will get in rally

definitions.text: What a crashed car will get
definitions.meaning: a breakdown truck tows the wrecked car away
to rally is to bounce back, as markets or patients do

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a car rally; 'rally' is in fact the second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrecked car gets towed by a breakdown service, and a rally is a revival.

clue.text: Did Dean get them on in a hurry?

definitions.text: Did Dean get them on in a hurry?

parts.words: Did Dean get them on in a hurry?
parts.note: Christopher Dean was a champion ice dancer, and to hurry is to get these on

explanation.walkthrough: Christopher Dean was a British Olympic ice-dancing champion; 'get your ... on' is an idiom for 'hurry up'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice dancers wear bladed boots, and the idiom for hurrying uses them.

parts.note: a hall is an entrance area of a house
a mark is a grade awarded

explanation.surface: Proof of authenticity for an entry grade.
explanation.definitionFit: A hallmark is the stamp certifying precious metal, hence any mark of authenticity.

parts.note: rag is a disparaging word for a newspaper
on means working or operating

explanation.surface: A newspaper in operation in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Aragon is a historic region and former kingdom in north-east Spain.

parts.note: B is the short form of British
in Australia a station is a large farm, much like a ranch

explanation.surface: A section of a small British railway station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'station' suggests a railway, but the Australian sense means a farm.
explanation.definitionFit: A branch is a part of a tree, firm or family.

clue.text: Place noted for its fair hair

definitions.meaning: a town north of London famous for its horse fair

explanation.walkthrough: Barnet is in north London, known for its old horse fair; in Cockney rhyming slang Barnet Fair means hair, shortened to Barnet.
explanation.definitionFit: Barnet is a London borough with a famous fair, and its name is slang for hair.

indicators.note: decorated suggests the letters are dressed up in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A conductor's music stand decorated with amber.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandmaster conducts a band, especially a military or brass band.

definitions.meaning: a collective noun for a group of women
bevvy is British slang for an alcoholic drink

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bevvy' is informal British for a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A bevy is a group of women, and the same sound is slang for a drink.

definitions.meaning: an old word for a dashing young man about town

explanation.walkthrough: 'Blood money' looks like one phrase; split it into two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: A buck is a dandy, also once called a blood, and slang for a dollar.

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like 'my!'
set means firm, as jelly sets

explanation.surface: My firm remains, leading into the next clue's famous British shop.
explanation.walkthrough: Read with the next clue: 'My firm' is Marks and Spencer, a British shop selling underwear. 'stays' is a noun: stiffening in women's underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Stays are a laced undergarment stiffened with bones, the same garment as a corset.

clue.text: … with old currency, supplier of ladies' underwear!

definitions.text: with old currency, supplier of ladies' underwear!

parts.words: with old currency, supplier of ladies' underwear!
parts.note: marks are an old German currency; joined with the surname they name the British high-street store

explanation.walkthrough: Marks and Spencer is a British department-store chain famous for its underwear; marks are old German money, so 'with old currency' supplies the other half of the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Marks and Spencer, colloquially with an S, is Britain's best-known seller of women's underwear.
